draft.title: The Constituent Assembly
card: The Constituent Assembly was a parliament meant to write a new constitution for Russia. The Provisional Government had promised it, and elections were held in November 1917, after the Bolsheviks took power.
The Socialist Revolutionaries won the most seats. The Bolsheviks won fewer than a quarter, so they did not have a majority.
The Assembly met once, in January 1918. It refused to accept the Bolshevik decrees and the authority of the Soviets, the councils the Bolsheviks used to govern.
The next day Bolshevik forces closed it, and it never met again. The Bolsheviks said the Soviets spoke for the people better than an elected assembly did.
draft.remember: The Bolsheviks lost the election, so they shut the Assembly and kept power.

a.q: Why did the Bolsheviks close the Constituent Assembly in January 1918?
opts: It would not accept their rule and they lacked a majority
It had finished writing the constitution they wanted
The Provisional Government had ordered it to be closed
It had voted to bring back the tsar to rule Russia
a.why: The Bolsheviks won fewer than a quarter of the seats, and the Assembly refused to back their decrees or the Soviets. They closed it to keep power. It had not finished any constitution, as it met only once.
a.clue: Think about who won the most seats in the election.

b.q: Which statement best describes what the closing of the Assembly showed about the Bolsheviks in early 1918?
opts: They put holding power ahead of the result of a free vote
They accepted the vote and shared power with the winners
They believed the Assembly had been elected unfairly
They wanted the Provisional Government to run the Assembly
b.why: The Assembly came from an election the Bolsheviks lost, and they shut it rather than accept the result. They did not share power. They claimed the Soviets were more representative, but that was a reason they gave, not proof the vote was unfair.
b.clue: Ask what the Bolsheviks did once the election result went against them.

a.best: It would not accept their rule and they lacked a majority

b.best: They put holding power ahead of the result of a free vote

check.summary: No problems found. The facts on the November 1917 elections, the SR win, the Bolsheviks' share of under a quarter, and the January 1918 closure check out, and both questions have one clearly right answer.
